# Quick Recap: Vectors 📊

```r
# Remember vectors? All elements same type
numbers <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
names <- c("Alice", "Bob", "Carol")
flags <- c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)

# Vectorized operations
numbers * 2         # 2 4 6 8 10
mean(numbers)       # 3
numbers[numbers > 3] # 4 5
```

::: {.callout-important}
**Today's Challenge:** What if we need to store different types together? Or organize data in 2D? That's where lists, matrices, and data frames come in! 🚀
:::

---

# Part 1: Lists - The Flexible Container

---

## What Are Lists?

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## Lists: R's Swiss Army Knife 🔧

Lists can hold **different types** of data, even other lists!
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
**Creating Lists**

```r
# Simple list
person <- list(
  name = "Alice",
  age = 25,
  scores = c(90, 85, 92),
  passed = TRUE
)

# Access by name
person$name      # "Alice"
person$age       # 25
person$scores    # 90 85 92

# Access by index
person[[1]]      # "Alice"
person[[3]]      # 90 85 92
```
:::

::: {.column}
**Why Lists?**

```r
# Vectors force one type
mixed_vec <- c(1, "two", TRUE)
mixed_vec
# "1" "two" "TRUE" - all character!

# Lists preserve types
mixed_list <- list(1, "two", TRUE)
mixed_list[[1]]  # numeric: 1
mixed_list[[2]]  # character: "two"
mixed_list[[3]]  # logical: TRUE

# Lists can be nested!
nested <- list(
  data = list(x = 1:5, y = 6:10),
  meta = list(source = "experiment")
)
```
:::
:::

## Interactive: List Builder 🎮

```{=html}
<!-- Global copy to clipboard function -->
<script>
function copyToClipboard(elementId, buttonElement) {
  const element = document.getElementById(elementId);
  const text = element.textContent;
  
  navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).then(function() {
    // Visual feedback
    const originalText = buttonElement.innerHTML;
    buttonElement.innerHTML = '✓ Copied!';
    buttonElement.classList.add('copied');
    
    setTimeout(function() {
      buttonElement.innerHTML = originalText;
      buttonElement.classList.remove('copied');
    }, 2000);
  }).catch(function(err) {
    console.error('Failed to copy:', err);
    buttonElement.innerHTML = '❌ Error';
    setTimeout(function() {
      buttonElement.innerHTML = '📋 Copy';
    }, 2000);
  });
}
</script>

<div class="interactive-tool">
  <h3>🔧 Interactive List Creator</h3>
  
  <div id="list-elements-container">
    <div class="list-element" data-id="0">
      <div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 2fr auto; gap: 8px; margin: 8px 0;">
        <input type="text" class="element-name" placeholder="name" value="name">
        <select class="element-type">
          <option value="character">Text</option>
          <option value="numeric">Number</option>
          <option value="logical">Logical</option>
          <option value="vector">Vector</option>
        </select>
        <input type="text" class="element-value" placeholder="value" value="Alice">
        <button onclick="removeListElement(0)" style="padding: 4px 8px; background: #e74c3c; color: white; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer;">✕</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  
  <div class="tool-buttons">
    <button class="tool-button secondary" onclick="addListElement()">➕ Add Element</button>
    <button class="tool-button" onclick="generateListCode()">Generate Code</button>
    <button class="tool-button secondary" onclick="showListOperations()">Show Operations</button>
    <button class="tool-button secondary" onclick="clearListTool()">Clear</button>
  </div>
  
  <div class="tool-output-container">
    <button class="copy-button" onclick="copyToClipboard('list-output', this)">📋 Copy</button>
    <div class="tool-output" id="list-output">Add elements and click "Generate Code"!</div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
let listElementCount = 1;

function addListElement() {
  const container = document.getElementById('list-elements-container');
  const newId = listElementCount++;
  
  const div = document.createElement('div');
  div.className = 'list-element';
  div.setAttribute('data-id', newId);
  div.innerHTML = `
    <div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 2fr auto; gap: 8px; margin: 8px 0;">
      <input type="text" class="element-name" placeholder="element${newId}">
      <select class="element-type">
        <option value="character">Text</option>
        <option value="numeric">Number</option>
        <option value="logical">Logical</option>
        <option value="vector">Vector</option>
      </select>
      <input type="text" class="element-value" placeholder="value">
      <button onclick="removeListElement(${newId})" style="padding: 4px 8px; background: #e74c3c; color: white; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer;">✕</button>
    </div>
  `;
  
  container.appendChild(div);
}

function removeListElement(id) {
  const element = document.querySelector(`.list-element[data-id="${id}"]`);
  if (element && document.querySelectorAll('.list-element').length > 1) {
    element.remove();
  }
}

function generateListCode() {
  const elements = document.querySelectorAll('.list-element');
  
  if (elements.length === 0) {
    document.getElementById('list-output').textContent = "❌ Add at least one element!";
    return;
  }
  
  let code = `# Creating a list\n`;
  code += `my_list <- list(\n`;
  
  const items = [];
  elements.forEach((elem, idx) => {
    const name = elem.querySelector('.element-name').value || `elem${idx+1}`;
    const type = elem.querySelector('.element-type').value;
    const value = elem.querySelector('.element-value').value;
    
    if (!value) return;
    
    let formattedValue;
    if (type === 'character') {
      formattedValue = `"${value}"`;
    } else if (type === 'numeric') {
      formattedValue = value;
    } else if (type === 'logical') {
      formattedValue = value.toUpperCase();
    } else if (type === 'vector') {
      formattedValue = `c(${value})`;
    }
    
    items.push(`  ${name} = ${formattedValue}`);
  });
  
  code += items.join(',\n');
  code += `\n)\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Accessing elements\n`;
  if (items.length > 0) {
    const firstName = items[0].split('=')[0].trim();
    code += `my_list$${firstName}      # By name\n`;
    code += `my_list[[1]]          # By index\n`;
    code += `my_list[["${firstName}"]]  # By name (alternative)\n\n`;
  }
  
  code += `# List information\n`;
  code += `names(my_list)        # Get element names\n`;
  code += `length(my_list)       # Number of elements: ${items.length}\n`;
  code += `str(my_list)          # Structure of list`;
  
  document.getElementById('list-output').textContent = code;
}

function showListOperations() {
  let code = `# Common List Operations\n\n`;
  code += `# Adding elements\n`;
  code += `my_list$new_element <- 100\n`;
  code += `my_list <- c(my_list, list(another = "value"))\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Removing elements\n`;
  code += `my_list$unwanted <- NULL\n`;
  code += `my_list[[3]] <- NULL\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Modifying elements\n`;
  code += `my_list$age <- 26  # Update\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Combining lists\n`;
  code += `list1 <- list(a = 1, b = 2)\n`;
  code += `list2 <- list(c = 3, d = 4)\n`;
  code += `combined <- c(list1, list2)\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Converting to vectors\n`;
  code += `unlist(my_list)  # Flatten to vector\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Applying functions\n`;
  code += `lapply(my_list, class)  # Class of each element`;
  
  document.getElementById('list-output').textContent = code;
}

function clearListTool() {
  document.getElementById('list-elements-container').innerHTML = `
    <div class="list-element" data-id="0">
      <div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 2fr auto; gap: 8px; margin: 8px 0;">
        <input type="text" class="element-name" placeholder="name" value="name">
        <select class="element-type">
          <option value="character">Text</option>
          <option value="numeric">Number</option>
          <option value="logical">Logical</option>
          <option value="vector">Vector</option>
        </select>
        <input type="text" class="element-value" placeholder="value" value="Alice">
        <button onclick="removeListElement(0)" style="padding: 4px 8px; background: #e74c3c; color: white; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer;">✕</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  `;
  listElementCount = 1;
  document.getElementById('list-output').textContent = 'Add elements and click "Generate Code"!';
}
</script>
```

# Part 2: Matrices - 2D Numeric Data

---

## Creating Matrices

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## Matrices: Rows × Columns of Numbers 🎯

Matrices are 2-dimensional arrays of **the same type** (usually numeric)
:::

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
**By Values**

```r
# Create matrix from vector
m <- matrix(
  1:12,           # Data
  nrow = 3,       # 3 rows
  ncol = 4        # 4 columns
)

m
#      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
# [1,]    1    4    7   10
# [2,]    2    5    8   11
# [3,]    3    6    9   12

# Fill by row instead
matrix(1:12, nrow=3, byrow=TRUE)
#      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
# [1,]    1    2    3    4
# [2,]    5    6    7    8
# [3,]    9   10   11   12
```
:::

::: {.column}
**By Binding Vectors**

```r
# Column binding
c1 <- c(1, 2, 3)
c2 <- c(4, 5, 6)
cbind(c1, c2)
#      c1 c2
# [1,]  1  4
# [2,]  2  5
# [3,]  3  6

# Row binding
r1 <- c(1, 2, 3)
r2 <- c(4, 5, 6)
rbind(r1, r2)
#    [,1] [,2] [,3]
# r1    1    2    3
# r2    4    5    6
```
:::
:::

---

## Matrix Operations

```r
# Create sample matrices
A <- matrix(1:6, nrow=2, ncol=3)
B <- matrix(7:12, nrow=2, ncol=3)

# Element-wise operations
A + B                # Add corresponding elements
A * B                # Multiply corresponding elements
A / B                # Divide corresponding elements

# Matrix multiplication (dimensions must match!)
C <- matrix(1:6, nrow=3, ncol=2)
A %*% C              # True matrix multiplication

# Transpose
t(A)                 # Flip rows and columns

# Other operations
nrow(A)              # Number of rows: 2
ncol(A)              # Number of columns: 3
dim(A)               # Dimensions: 2 3
```

---

## Accessing Matrix Elements

```r
# Create matrix
m <- matrix(1:12, nrow=3, ncol=4)

# Single element
m[1, 2]              # Row 1, Column 2: 4
m[3, 4]              # Row 3, Column 4: 12

# Entire row or column
m[1, ]               # First row: 1 4 7 10
m[, 2]               # Second column: 4 5 6

# Multiple rows/columns
m[1:2, ]             # Rows 1-2
m[, c(1, 3)]         # Columns 1 and 3

# Submatrix
m[1:2, 2:3]          # Top-left 2×2 of middle columns

# With row/column names
colnames(m) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")
rownames(m) <- c("X", "Y", "Z")
m["X", "B"]          # Access by name: 4
```

---

## Interactive: Matrix Builder 🎮

```{=html}
<div class="interactive-tool">
  <h3>🎯 Matrix Creator & Visualizer</h3>
  
  <div class="tool-controls">
    <div class="control-group">
      <label>Number of Rows:</label>
      <input type="number" id="matrix-rows" value="3" min="1" max="6">
    </div>
    
    <div class="control-group">
      <label>Number of Columns:</label>
      <input type="number" id="matrix-cols" value="4" min="1" max="6">
    </div>
    
    <div class="control-group">
      <label>Fill Method:</label>
      <select id="matrix-fill">
        <option value="sequence">Sequence (1, 2, 3...)</option>
        <option value="random">Random (1-100)</option>
        <option value="custom">Custom Values</option>
      </select>
    </div>
    
    <div class="control-group" id="custom-values-group" style="display: none;">
      <label>Values (comma-separated):</label>
      <input type="text" id="matrix-values" placeholder="1,2,3,4,5,6...">
    </div>
    
    <div class="control-group">
      <label>Fill Direction:</label>
      <select id="matrix-direction">
        <option value="column">By Column (default)</option>
        <option value="row">By Row</option>
      </select>
    </div>
  </div>
  
  <div class="tool-buttons">
    <button class="tool-button" onclick="createMatrix()">Create Matrix</button>
    <button class="tool-button secondary" onclick="showMatrixOperations()">Show Operations</button>
    <button class="tool-button secondary" onclick="clearMatrixTool()">Clear</button>
  </div>
  
  <div class="tool-output-container">
    <button class="copy-button" onclick="copyToClipboard('matrix-output', this)">📋 Copy</button>
    <div class="tool-output" id="matrix-output">Configure and click "Create Matrix"!</div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
document.getElementById('matrix-fill').addEventListener('change', function() {
  document.getElementById('custom-values-group').style.display = 
    this.value === 'custom' ? 'block' : 'none';
});

function createMatrix() {
  const rows = parseInt(document.getElementById('matrix-rows').value);
  const cols = parseInt(document.getElementById('matrix-cols').value);
  const fill = document.getElementById('matrix-fill').value;
  const direction = document.getElementById('matrix-direction').value;
  
  if (rows < 1 || cols < 1 || rows > 6 || cols > 6) {
    document.getElementById('matrix-output').textContent = 
      "❌ Please enter valid dimensions (1-6)!";
    return;
  }
  
  let values = [];
  const totalElements = rows * cols;
  
  if (fill === 'sequence') {
    values = Array.from({length: totalElements}, (_, i) => i + 1);
  } else if (fill === 'random') {
    values = Array.from({length: totalElements}, () => Math.floor(Math.random() * 100) + 1);
  } else if (fill === 'custom') {
    const customStr = document.getElementById('matrix-values').value;
    values = customStr.split(',').map(x => parseFloat(x.trim())).filter(x => !isNaN(x));
    
    if (values.length !== totalElements) {
      document.getElementById('matrix-output').textContent = 
        `❌ Need exactly ${totalElements} values for ${rows}×${cols} matrix!`;
      return;
    }
  }
  
  // Create matrix visualization
  let matrix;
  if (direction === 'column') {
    matrix = Array(rows).fill(0).map(() => Array(cols).fill(0));
    let idx = 0;
    for (let col = 0; col < cols; col++) {
      for (let row = 0; row < rows; row++) {
        matrix[row][col] = values[idx++];
      }
    }
  } else {
    matrix = Array(rows).fill(0).map(() => Array(cols).fill(0));
    let idx = 0;
    for (let row = 0; row < rows; row++) {
      for (let col = 0; col < cols; col++) {
        matrix[row][col] = values[idx++];
      }
    }
  }
  
  // Generate code
  let code = `# Creating a ${rows}×${cols} matrix\n`;
  code += `m <- matrix(\n`;
  code += `  c(${values.join(', ')}),\n`;
  code += `  nrow = ${rows},\n`;
  code += `  ncol = ${cols}`;
  
  if (direction === 'row') {
    code += `,\n  byrow = TRUE`;
  }
  
  code += `\n)\n\n`;
  
  // Show matrix
  code += `# Result:\n`;
  code += `#      `;
  for (let col = 0; col < cols; col++) {
    code += `[,${col+1}]`.padEnd(6);
  }
  code += `\n`;
  
  for (let row = 0; row < rows; row++) {
    code += `# [${row+1},] `;
    for (let col = 0; col < cols; col++) {
      code += `${matrix[row][col]}`.padEnd(6);
    }
    code += `\n`;
  }
  
  code += `\n# Matrix dimensions: ${rows} rows × ${cols} columns`;
  
  document.getElementById('matrix-output').textContent = code;
}

function showMatrixOperations() {
  const rows = parseInt(document.getElementById('matrix-rows').value);
  const cols = parseInt(document.getElementById('matrix-cols').value);
  
  let code = `# Matrix Operations Guide\n\n`;
  code += `# Accessing elements\n`;
  code += `m[1, 2]              # Element at row 1, col 2\n`;
  code += `m[1, ]               # Entire first row\n`;
  code += `m[, 2]               # Entire second column\n`;
  code += `m[1:2, ]             # First two rows\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Matrix information\n`;
  code += `dim(m)               # Dimensions: ${rows} ${cols}\n`;
  code += `nrow(m)              # Number of rows: ${rows}\n`;
  code += `ncol(m)              # Number of columns: ${cols}\n`;
  code += `length(m)            # Total elements: ${rows * cols}\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Statistical operations\n`;
  code += `rowSums(m)           # Sum of each row\n`;
  code += `colSums(m)           # Sum of each column\n`;
  code += `rowMeans(m)          # Mean of each row\n`;
  code += `colMeans(m)          # Mean of each column\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Transformations\n`;
  code += `t(m)                 # Transpose\n`;
  code += `m * 2                # Multiply all by 2\n`;
  code += `m + 10               # Add 10 to all\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Adding row/column names\n`;
  code += `rownames(m) <- c("R1", "R2", ...)\n`;
  code += `colnames(m) <- c("C1", "C2", ...)`;
  
  document.getElementById('matrix-output').textContent = code;
}

function clearMatrixTool() {
  document.getElementById('matrix-rows').value = '3';
  document.getElementById('matrix-cols').value = '4';
  document.getElementById('matrix-fill').selectedIndex = 0;
  document.getElementById('matrix-direction').selectedIndex = 0;
  document.getElementById('matrix-values').value = '';
  document.getElementById('custom-values-group').style.display = 'none';
  document.getElementById('matrix-output').textContent = 'Configure and click "Create Matrix"!';
}
</script>
```

# Part 3: Data Frames - The Star of R! ⭐

---

## What Are Data Frames?

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
**Data Frames: Excel-like Tables in R** 📊

Think of data frames as spreadsheets:
- **Rows** = observations/cases
- **Columns** = variables (can be different types!)
- Each column is actually a vector
:::

```r
# Creating a data frame
students <- data.frame(
  name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "David"),
  age = c(20, 22, 21, 23),
  score = c(85, 92, 78, 95),
  passed = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)
)

students
#     name age score passed
# 1  Alice  20    85   TRUE
# 2    Bob  22    92   TRUE
# 3  Carol  21    78   TRUE
# 4  David  23    95   TRUE
```

---

## Why Data Frames Are Amazing

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
**Mixed Data Types** 🎨

```r
# Different types per column!
df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3,
  name = c("A", "B", "C"),
  value = c(10.5, 20.3, 15.7),
  flag = c(T, F, T)
)

# Check types
str(df)
# 'data.frame': 3 obs of 4 vars
#  $ id   : int  1 2 3
#  $ name : chr  "A" "B" "C"
#  $ value: num  10.5 20.3 15.7
#  $ flag : logi  TRUE FALSE TRUE
```
:::

::: {.column}
**Easy Access** 🎯

```r
# Access columns
df$name          # Vector of names
df[, "value"]    # Same as above
df[[2]]          # Second column

# Access rows
df[1, ]          # First row
df[c(1,3), ]     # Rows 1 and 3

# Subset
df[df$value > 15, ]
# Rows where value > 15

# Single cell
df[2, 3]         # Row 2, Column 3
```
:::
:::

---

```{=html}
<script>

const dfTemplates = {

    {name: "price", type: "numeric", values: "19.99, 24.50, 12.75"},
    {name: "in_stock", type: "logical", values: "TRUE, TRUE, FALSE"}
  ],
  experiments: [
    {name: "trial", type: "integer", values: "1, 2, 3, 4, 5"},
    {name: "treatment", type: "character", values: "A, B, A, B, Control"},
    {name: "result", type: "numeric", values: "7.2, 8.1, 7.5, 8.3, 6.9"},
    {name: "success", type: "logical", values: "TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE"}
  ]
};

function loadDataFrameTemplate() {
  const template = document.getElementById('df-template').value;
  if (!template) return;
  
  const data = dfTemplates[template];
  const container = document.getElementById('df-columns-container');
  container.innerHTML = '';
  dfColumnCount = 0;
  
  data.forEach(col => {
    const id = dfColumnCount++;
    const div = document.createElement('div');
    div.className = 'df-column';
    div.setAttribute('data-id', id);
    div.innerHTML = `
      <div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.5fr 1fr 3fr auto; gap: 8px; margin: 8px 0; align-items: center;">
        <input type="text" class="df-col-name" value="${col.name}">
        <select class="df-col-type">
          <option value="integer" ${col.type === 'integer' ? 'selected' : ''}>Integer</option>
          <option value="numeric" ${col.type === 'numeric' ? 'selected' : ''}>Numeric</option>
          <option value="character" ${col.type === 'character' ? 'selected' : ''}>Character</option>
          <option value="logical" ${col.type === 'logical' ? 'selected' : ''}>Logical</option>
        </select>
        <input type="text" class="df-col-values" value="${col.values}">
        <button onclick="removeDFColumn(${id})" style="padding: 4px 8px; background: #e74c3c; color: white; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer;">✕</button>
      </div>
    `;
    container.appendChild(div);
  });
}

function addDFColumn() {
  const container = document.getElementById('df-columns-container');
  const newId = dfColumnCount++;
  
  const div = document.createElement('div');
  div.className = 'df-column';
  div.setAttribute('data-id', newId);
  div.innerHTML = `
    <div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.5fr 1fr 3fr auto; gap: 8px; margin: 8px 0; align-items: center;">
      <input type="text" class="df-col-name" placeholder="col${newId}">
      <select class="df-col-type">
        <option value="integer">Integer</option>
        <option value="numeric">Numeric</option>
        <option value="character">Character</option>
        <option value="logical">Logical</option>
      </select>
      <input type="text" class="df-col-values" placeholder="1, 2, 3">
      <button onclick="removeDFColumn(${newId})" style="padding: 4px 8px; background: #e74c3c; color: white; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer;">✕</button>
    </div>
  `;
  
  container.appendChild(div);
}

function removeDFColumn(id) {
  const element = document.querySelector(`.df-column[data-id="${id}"]`);
  if (element && document.querySelectorAll('.df-column').length > 1) {
    element.remove();
  }
}

function generateDataFrameCode() {
  const columns = document.querySelectorAll('.df-column');
  
  if (columns.length === 0) {
    document.getElementById('df-output').textContent = "❌ Add at least one column!";
    return;
  }
  
  let code = `# Creating a data frame\n`;
  code += `df <- data.frame(\n`;
  
  const colDefs = [];
  const colData = {};
  let maxLength = 0;
  
  columns.forEach((col, idx) => {
    const name = col.querySelector('.df-col-name').value || `col${idx+1}`;
    const type = col.querySelector('.df-col-type').value;
    const valuesStr = col.querySelector('.df-col-values').value;
    
    if (!valuesStr) return;
    
    const values = valuesStr.split(',').map(v => v.trim());
    maxLength = Math.max(maxLength, values.length);
    colData[name] = {type, values};
    
    let formattedValues;
    if (type === 'character') {
      formattedValues = values.map(v => `"${v}"`).join(', ');
    } else if (type === 'logical') {
      formattedValues = values.map(v => v.toUpperCase()).join(', ');
    } else {
      formattedValues = values.join(', ');
    }
    
    colDefs.push(`  ${name} = c(${formattedValues})`);
  });
  
  code += colDefs.join(',\n');
  code += `\n)\n\n`;
  
  // Show data frame
  code += `# Result (first few rows):\n`;
  code += `#   `;
  Object.keys(colData).forEach(name => {
    code += name.padEnd(12);
  });
  code += `\n`;
  
  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(maxLength, 4); i++) {
    code += `# ${(i+1)} `;
    Object.keys(colData).forEach(name => {
      const val = colData[name].values[i] || 'NA';
      code += val.padEnd(12);
    });
    code += `\n`;
  }
  
  code += `\n# Data frame: ${maxLength} observations, ${Object.keys(colData).length} variables`;
  
  document.getElementById('df-output').textContent = code;
}

function showDFOperations() {
  let code = `# Essential Data Frame Operations\n\n`;
  code += `# Viewing data\n`;
  code += `head(df)              # First 6 rows\n`;
  code += `tail(df)              # Last 6 rows\n`;
  code += `View(df)              # Open in viewer (RStudio)\n`;
  code += `str(df)               # Structure summary\n`;
  code += `summary(df)           # Statistical summary\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Accessing columns\n`;
  code += `df$column_name        # By name (vector)\n`;
  code += `df[["column_name"]]   # By name (alternative)\n`;
  code += `df[, 2]               # By index\n`;
  code += `df[, c("col1", "col2")] # Multiple columns\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Subsetting rows\n`;
  code += `df[1:3, ]             # Rows 1-3\n`;
  code += `df[df$age > 20, ]     # Conditional\n`;
  code += `subset(df, age > 20)  # Using subset()\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Adding columns\n`;
  code += `df$new_col <- values\n`;
  code += `df <- cbind(df, new_col)\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Removing columns\n`;
  code += `df$unwanted <- NULL\n`;
  code += `df <- df[, -3]        # Remove 3rd column\n\n`;
  
  code += `# Dimensions\n`;
  code += `nrow(df)              # Number of rows\n`;
  code += `ncol(df)              # Number of columns\n`;
  code += `dim(df)               # Both dimensions`;
  
  document.getElementById('df-output').textContent = code;
}

function clearDFTool() {
  document.getElementById('df-template').selectedIndex = 0;
  document.getElementById('df-columns-container').innerHTML = `
    <div class="df-column" data-id="0">
      <div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.5fr 1fr 3fr auto; gap: 8px; margin: 8px 0; align-items: center;">
        <input type="text" class="df-col-name" placeholder="col_name" value="id">
        <select class="df-col-type">
          <option value="integer">Integer</option>
          <option value="numeric">Numeric</option>
          <option value="character">Character</option>
          <option value="logical">Logical</option>
        </select>
        <input type="text" class="df-col-values" placeholder="values (comma-separated)" value="1, 2, 3">
        <button onclick="removeDFColumn(0)" style="padding: 4px 8px; background: #e74c3c; color: white; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer;">✕</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  `;
  dfColumnCount = 1;
  document.getElementById('df-output').textContent = 'Configure columns and click "Generate Code"!';
}
</script>
```

# Part 4: Reading Data Files 📁

## Reading CSV Files

::: {.callout-tip icon="true"}
## CSV: Comma-Separated Values 📄

Most common format for sharing data!
:::

```r
# Reading a CSV file
data <- read.csv("mydata.csv")

# Common options
data <- read.csv(
  "mydata.csv",
  header = TRUE,        # First row is column names
  sep = ",",            # Separator (comma)
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,  # Keep strings as text
  na.strings = c("NA", "")   # What counts as missing?
)

# Quick peek
head(data)              # First 6 rows
summary(data)           # Statistical summary

# Using tidyverse (better!)
library(readr)
data <- read_csv("mydata.csv")  # Smarter defaults!
```

# Quick Challenge! 🧠

## Challenge 1: Data Frame Access

```{=html}
<div class="quiz-box">
  <div class="quiz-question">What's the best way to access the "age" column in a data frame called `students`?</div>
  
  <div class="quiz-options">
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkDFQuiz(this, false)">students[age]</div>
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkDFQuiz(this, true)">students$age</div>
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkDFQuiz(this, false)">students.age</div>
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkDFQuiz(this, false)">students->age</div>
  </div>
  
  <div id="df-quiz-feedback" style="display: none;"></div>
</div>

<script>
function checkDFQuiz(element, isCorrect) {
  document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-option').forEach(opt => {
    opt.classList.remove('correct', 'incorrect');
  });
  
  element.classList.add(isCorrect ? 'correct' : 'incorrect');
  
  const feedback = document.getElementById('df-quiz-feedback');
  feedback.style.display = 'block';
  feedback.className = 'quiz-feedback ' + (isCorrect ? 'correct' : 'incorrect');
  
  if (isCorrect) {
    feedback.textContent = '✅ Correct! The $ operator is the most common and readable way to access columns by name.';
  } else {
    feedback.textContent = '❌ Not quite! Use the $ operator: students$age. Square brackets need quotes: students[["age"]]';
  }
}
</script>
```

---

## Challenge 2: Matrix Dimensions

```{=html}
<div class="quiz-box">
  <div class="quiz-question">What are the dimensions of: <code>matrix(1:12, nrow=4)</code>?</div>
  
  <div class="quiz-options">
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkMatrixQuiz(this, false)">3 rows × 4 columns</div>
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkMatrixQuiz(this, true)">4 rows × 3 columns</div>
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkMatrixQuiz(this, false)">12 rows × 1 column</div>
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkMatrixQuiz(this, false)">1 row × 12 columns</div>
  </div>
  
  <div id="matrix-quiz-feedback" style="display: none;"></div>
</div>

<script>
function checkMatrixQuiz(element, isCorrect) {
  document.querySelectorAll('#matrix-quiz-feedback').forEach(f => f.previousElementSibling.querySelectorAll('.quiz-option').forEach(opt => {
    opt.classList.remove('correct', 'incorrect');
  }));
  
  element.classList.add(isCorrect ? 'correct' : 'incorrect');
  
  const feedback = document.getElementById('matrix-quiz-feedback');
  feedback.style.display = 'block';
  feedback.className = 'quiz-feedback ' + (isCorrect ? 'correct' : 'incorrect');
  
  if (isCorrect) {
    feedback.textContent = '✅ Correct! 12 elements ÷ 4 rows = 3 columns. Matrices fill by column by default.';
  } else {
    feedback.textContent = '❌ Try again! With nrow=4 and 12 elements, you get 4 rows and 3 columns.';
  }
}
</script>
```

## Challenge 3: List vs Data Frame

```{=html}
<div class="quiz-box">
  <div class="quiz-question">When should you use a list instead of a data frame?</div>
  
  <div class="quiz-options">
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkListQuiz(this, false)">When all elements are the same length</div>
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkListQuiz(this, true)">When storing different-length vectors or complex objects</div>
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkListQuiz(this, false)">When all data is numeric</div>
    <div class="quiz-option" onclick="checkListQuiz(this, false)">Lists and data frames are identical</div>
  </div>
  
  <div id="list-quiz-feedback" style="display: none;"></div>
</div>

<script>
function checkListQuiz(element, isCorrect) {
  document.querySelectorAll('#list-quiz-feedback').forEach(f => f.previousElementSibling.querySelectorAll('.quiz-option').forEach(opt => {
    opt.classList.remove('correct', 'incorrect');
  }));
  
  element.classList.add(isCorrect ? 'correct' : 'incorrect');
  
  const feedback = document.getElementById('list-quiz-feedback');
  feedback.style.display = 'block';
  feedback.className = 'quiz-feedback ' + (isCorrect ? 'correct' : 'incorrect');
  
  if (isCorrect) {
    feedback.textContent = '✅ Correct! Lists are flexible — perfect for storing models, mixed objects, or different-length vectors.';
  } else {
    feedback.textContent = '❌ Not quite! Lists are best when you need flexibility: different lengths, nested structures, or model outputs.';
  }
}
</script>
```

# Comparing Data Structures 📊

| Structure | Dimensions | Same Type? | Use Case |
|-----------|------------|------------|----------|
| **Vector** | 1D | ✅ Yes | Single variable |
| **List** | 1D | ❌ No | Mixed types, complex objects |
| **Matrix** | 2D | ✅ Yes | Numeric calculations |
| **Data Frame** | 2D | ❌ No | **Most data analysis** |

::: {.callout-important}
**Key Insight:** Data frames are your go-to for most data science work! They're like spreadsheets with superpowers. 💪
:::
